note: CKEditor Abbreviation is a CKEditor 5 plugin (mostly JS; only PHP is hook_help). Declared in ckeditor_abbreviation.ckeditor5.yml: CKEditor5 plugin id 'ckeditor_abbreviation_abbreviation', JS plugin 'abbreviation.Abbreviation', toolbar item id 'abbreviation', elements '<abbr>' and '<abbr title>'. No settings form, no config schema, no permissions, no configure route. It is enabled by adding the 'abbreviation' toolbar item to a text format's CKEditor 5 toolbar (editor.editor.<format> -> settings.toolbar.items) and allowing <abbr title> in that format's filter_html. Medium/hard cases create dedicated CKEditor 5 text formats (ckabbr_*) and read/write editor.editor.<format> config; verify checks the toolbar items array contains 'abbreviation'.

evals.prompt: I installed the ckeditor_abbreviation module on Drupal 11 but the Abbreviation button doesn't appear when editing content. There's no settings page for the module. How do I actually enable the Abbreviation button for a text format?
evals.expected_output: It has no settings form. Edit a text format that uses CKEditor 5 (Configuration -> Content authoring -> Text formats and editors), drag the Abbreviation button from Available buttons into the Active toolbar, and save. In config this adds the 'abbreviation' toolbar item to editor.editor.<format> -> settings.toolbar.items.

evals.prompt: What HTML does the ckeditor_abbreviation CKEditor 5 button produce, and what must I allow in the 'Limit allowed HTML tags' filter so the tooltip/explanation is kept?
evals.expected_output: The plugin produces <abbr> elements, and <abbr title> for the explanation. Its ckeditor5.yml declares elements <abbr> and <abbr title>. To keep the tooltip you must allow <abbr title> in the format's filter_html allowed_html list.

evals.prompt: For the ckeditor_abbreviation module, what is the CKEditor 5 toolbar item id you add to a format's toolbar to enable the button, and which underlying CKEditor 5 JS plugin does it load? (See its *.ckeditor5.yml.)
evals.expected_output: The toolbar item id is 'abbreviation' (defined under drupal.toolbar_items in ckeditor_abbreviation.ckeditor5.yml). The plugin definition id is ckeditor_abbreviation_abbreviation, which loads the JS plugin abbreviation.Abbreviation.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, exactly one text format has the CKEditor Abbreviation button enabled on its CKEditor 5 toolbar. Inspect the live editor configuration and name that text format's machine name.
evals.expected_output: The format is ckabbr_known: editor.editor.ckabbr_known -> settings.toolbar.items contains 'abbreviation'. Find it e.g. with: drush cget editor.editor.ckabbr_known settings.toolbar.items

evals.prompt: The text format 'ckabbr_html' on this site uses the CKEditor Abbreviation button. Inspect its live filter configuration and confirm whether the abbreviation tooltip (the title attribute on abbr) will survive HTML filtering — quote the relevant allowed-HTML entry.
evals.expected_output: Yes: filter.format.ckabbr_html -> filters.filter_html.settings.allowed_html includes '<abbr title>', so the title attribute (the tooltip explanation) is preserved. Read with: drush cget filter.format.ckabbr_html filters.filter_html.settings.allowed_html

evals.prompt: On this site there is a CKEditor 5 text format with machine name 'ckabbr_task' whose toolbar currently has only bold and italic. Using the ckeditor_abbreviation module, enable its Abbreviation button on this format's toolbar and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add the 'abbreviation' toolbar item to editor.editor.ckabbr_task -> settings.toolbar.items and save (e.g. load the Editor entity, push 'abbreviation' onto settings.toolbar.items, save). verify passes when the items array contains 'abbreviation'.

evals.prompt: On this site the CKEditor 5 text format 'ckabbr_title' already has the Abbreviation button, but abbreviations added with it lose their tooltip because its 'Limit allowed HTML tags' filter strips the title attribute. Update this format so the abbreviation explanation (the title attribute on abbr) is preserved, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add '<abbr title>' to filter.format.ckabbr_title -> filters.filter_html.settings.allowed_html and save, so the title attribute on <abbr> is allowed. verify passes when the allowed_html permits title on abbr.
